solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hesitate with clutch before finding reverse

indicators.note: before places the clutching word ahead of the reverse word in the answer

parts.note: to clutch something is to hold it
to reverse is to go back

explanation.surface: A nervous driver dithers, foot on the clutch, before finding reverse gear.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold back is to refrain or delay acting, which is what someone who hesitates does.

clue.text: Threaten head of government in royal house

indicators.note: in places that opening letter inside the name of the royal house

parts.note: Hanover was the German royal house that ruled Britain from George I to Victoria

indicators.note: head of takes just the opening letter of the word government

explanation.surface: A threat to the government is said to come from within the royal household.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that hangs over you looms as a threat, so the phrase is an idiom for threaten.

clue.text: Circles vowel in error

parts.note: circuits of a track are laps
E is one of the five vowels

explanation.surface: Someone marks rings around a vowel that was wrongly written.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slip or small mistake, a synonym for an error.

clue.text: Sold illicitly from sack on stage

indicators.note: in a down answer, on puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: to give someone the sack or the boot both mean dismissal
a stage of a journey or race is a leg

explanation.surface: Goods sold illegally come from someone dismissed from a stage production.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootleg describes goods, especially liquor or recordings, made or sold illegally.

clue.text: Unfriendly clubs of long standing

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit
something of long standing is old

explanation.surface: Golf clubs that have been around for ages are not very welcoming.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold manner is distant and unwelcoming, a synonym for unfriendly.

clue.text: Oriental language used by Roman churchmen

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An Eastern tongue is spoken by priests of the Roman Catholic Church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used by' signals that the answer sits within RomAN CHUrchmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Manchu is the Tungusic language of the Manchu people of northeast China, an Oriental tongue.

clue.text: Further down payment

definitions.meaning: to further a cause is to promote or move it forward
money paid up front before the rest is due

explanation.definitionFit: Advance means both to promote something and money paid ahead of time.

clue.text: A short time after US state capital makes a pact

indicators.note: after puts the short time phrase behind the state capital

parts.note: Concord is the capital of New Hampshire
T is the standard short form of time

explanation.surface: Shortly after arriving at a US state capital, a deal is struck.
explanation.definitionFit: A concordat is a formal agreement, especially one between a government and the Vatican.

clue.text: Use fan — if faulty it could be dangerous

indicators.note: faulty means broken, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that using a broken fan could be hazardous.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsafe poses a risk, so it is a synonym for dangerous.

clue.text: Not one puzzle that's all right

parts.note: no means not one, as in no sign
a puzzle to solve is a problem

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a puzzle as no trouble at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a casual reply meaning the request causes no difficulty, just as saying that's all right does.

clue.text: Small cars go for service

parts.note: Minis are small British cars
to have a go is to have a try

explanation.surface: Small cars are taken in for a service at the garage.
explanation.definitionFit: A ministry is a government department or a period of religious service, as in a priest's ministry.

clue.text: Extremely visible star? On the contrary, a planet

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the outside letters of visible are taken
the opposite way round, so the word for the star is read backwards

parts.note: the sun is our nearest star

explanation.surface: Someone spots a bright star, only to be told it is really a planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' gives VE from visible; 'On the contrary' turns SUN into NUS. The surface jokes that this bright evening light looks like a star but is a planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus is the second planet from the sun, often mistaken for a star.

clue.text: Number attending poorly US playwright

indicators.note: attending means going along with, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: one is a number
poorly means ill

explanation.surface: Several people turn up to see a sick American dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene O'Neill was a Nobel-winning American dramatist, author of Long Day's Journey into Night.

clue.text: Working, also away, periodically

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
and means also
away means off, as in a day off

explanation.surface: Someone works only part of the time, away the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: On and off means intermittently, at irregular intervals, which is what periodically means here.

clue.text: All the things one would like to happen whilst travelling round island

definitions.text: All the things one would like to happen

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters surround the island piece
travelling suggests moving about, so the letters of whilst are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone dreams of everything they'd like while touring an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' gives WHLIST, and 'round' wraps those letters about the island abbreviation just after their first letter; one I comes from each source.
explanation.definitionFit: A wish list is an inventory of things one hopes to get or see happen.

clue.text: Arranged stage opening of 'Roots', as a substitute, in a W Sussex town

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the letters of stage are rearranged
opening of takes the first letter of the word Roots

parts.note: instead means in place of, as a substitute

explanation.surface: A theatre opening of the play Roots was staged as a substitute in a Sussex town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' turns STAGE into EASTG. EAST GRINSTEAD is a market town in West Sussex, southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: East Grinstead is a town in the county of West Sussex, in southern England.

clue.text: Struggle for air, as cut off working on far side of mine

indicators.note: working means being worked into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged
far side of takes the last letter of the word mine

explanation.surface: A miner, cut off at the far end of a mine, gasps for breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges ASCUTOFF into SUFFOCAT, and 'far side of' adds E from mine.
explanation.definitionFit: To suffocate is to be unable to breathe, struggling for air.

clue.text: Offer of support also broadcast

parts.note: a prop is a support

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters of also are rearranged

explanation.surface: An offer of backing is also announced on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal is something put forward for acceptance, an offer.

clue.text: Cleaner in 'Father Ted', sure eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd housekeeper appears in the sitcom Father Ted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges FATHER TED SURE. Father Ted is a 1990s British-Irish sitcom about priests, whose housekeeper Mrs Doyle is famously odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A feather duster is a cleaning tool, so it is a cleaner in the sense of an implement.

clue.text: Resolute, a worker crossing barrier

indicators.note: crossing means the barrier piece lies across, sitting within the other letters

parts.note: a worker ant is the classic crossword worker
a dam is a barrier across water

explanation.surface: A determined worker clambers over a barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant means unshakeable in resolve, a synonym for resolute.

clue.text: Ignorant one in Paris perhaps describing a state of conflict

indicators.note: describing in its sense of drawing round means the French word encloses the rest

parts.note: une is French for one, Paris being a French example
war is a state of armed conflict

explanation.surface: A Parisian is unaware that a war has broken out.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unaware of something means not knowing it, which is to be ignorant of it.

clue.text: Exhausted American editor on horseback

parts.note: a jockey who is mounted is said to be up

explanation.surface: A US newspaper editor, worn out, rides a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Used up means consumed or spent, so also tired out, a synonym for exhausted.

clue.text: Nervous picadors scattered

indicators.note: nervous means agitated, so the letters of picadors are rearranged

explanation.surface: Jittery bullfighters on horseback flee in all directions.
explanation.walkthrough: Picadors are the mounted lancers in a bullfight; 'Nervous' rearranges their letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporadic means occurring at scattered, irregular intervals or places.

clue.text: Governor's role when recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the two words are read backwards together

parts.note: an actor's role is a part
as can mean when, as in as he arrived

explanation.surface: A governor's position is remembered when he is recalled from office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns PART AS into SA TRAP. The 's of 'Governor's' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a provincial governor in ancient Persia, and the word now means any petty ruler.

clue.text: Check about first of Georges to rule as monarch

indicators.note: about means the restraining word goes round the next letter

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of Georges

explanation.surface: A check on the early King Georges limited their royal power.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to hold royal office, to rule as a king or queen.

clue.text: Hide small family

parts.note: kin means family

explanation.surface: A small family goes into hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: Hide in its noun sense is an animal's skin.

clue.text: Small drop of Scotch before opening of Ayckbourn play

indicators.note: before puts the whisky ahead of the next letter

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of whisky

indicators.note: opening of takes the first letter of Ayckbourn

explanation.surface: A theatregoer takes a nip of whisky before the first night of an Ayckbourn comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Ayckbourn is a prolific English playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play for the stage, television or radio.

clue.text: Get the wrong idea from a young lady escort, initially

indicators.note: initially means the escorting word comes first in the answer

parts.note: to escort someone somewhere is to take them
a miss is a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A young lady misreads her escort's intentions at the start of the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks like a first-letter signal, but it just places the escort word at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something amiss is to misinterpret it, especially as an offence.

clue.text: Rather charming to look at

definitions.meaning: rather means fairly, as in fairly good

explanation.definitionFit: Pretty means both fairly, as an adverb, and attractive, as an adjective.

clue.text: Deduce article backing league's leader is extremely annoying

parts.note: to deduce is to infer

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the article is read in reverse

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word league

explanation.surface: Someone works out that the league's article attacking its chairman is very irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns AN into NA; 'leader' gives L from league's.
explanation.definitionFit: Infernal literally means hellish, and colloquially it means dreadfully irritating.
